title: Abba, Father of Rabbi Simlai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 5:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Pesachim.5.3.5): Hyman writes that Abba’s son Rabbi Simlai asked Rabbi Yochanan to teach him aggadah. Rabbi Yochanan refused, saying that Simlai was from Nehardea and lived in the South. In [Pesachim 62b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.62b.8) it is the reverse: that he was from Lod and his place of residence was Nehardea. Hyman prefers the Jerusalem Talmud’s reading, which he considers proven by [Rosh Hashanah 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.20b.3), where Abba, the father of Rabbi Simlai, said to Shmuel: “Does the Master know this matter that was taught in the secret of intercalation?” — and it is known that Shmuel was in Nehardea. In Pesachim there, where he came before Rabbi Yochanan, Hyman proposes “before Rabbi Yonatan,” as in the Jerusalem Talmud. His son Rabbi Simlai was a student of Rabbi Yehudah Nesia; Hyman therefore places his father at the end of the days of the Tannaim, after Rabbi.[^1]

notes.text: The Jerusalem Talmud names Rabbi Yonatan and gives Nehardea as Simlai’s origin and the South as his residence. The Bavli names Rabbi Yochanan and gives Lod as his origin and Nehardea as his residence. Hyman uses Abba’s conversation with Shmuel to argue for the Jerusalem Talmud’s account.
